### [The book (in Dutch)](../manuscript/index.html){hreflang="nl"}

<!-- MIEKE: "Eerst de spanning eruit, dan de stof erin." Gekozen: "First the tension out, then

*De regressieve ruggengraat* — *The Regressive Backbone* — is a statistics textbook with the working notes left in: at the bottom of every page you can see where the author is still weighing things up, and where he still has his doubts. First the tension out, then the subject in. It is being written in Dutch, and you can read along as it grows. The first four chapters are on their way in English, with an R exercise book that walks alongside them.
:::

::: {.cc-card .cc-card-tabellen}
### [Tables &amp; *p*-values](../tables/index.html)

<!-- BEN: de verwijzing naar de (Nederlandse) speelkist is weggelaten; het Engelse menu wijst
     alleen naar wat er in het Engels is. -->
A test statistic from a paper — *t*(38) = 2.24, *z* = 1.96 — and you see the *p*-value straight away, as an **area** under the curve, with the *z*, *t*, *F* and χ² tables beside it. A tool, not a toy.
:::

::: {.cc-card .cc-card-solomon}
### [The judgement of Solomon](../speeltjes/solomon-en.html)

<!-- MIEKE: "sensitisatie" — gekozen "sensitisation" (Brits). De speeltjesbladzij zelf schrijft

Four groups, one therapy, and a pretest that does something of its own. You take the improvement in group I apart, step by step, into four pieces, until only the sensitisation is left — and then you see that it was a regression all along.
:::

## The doubt is left in

Statistics is the subject that takes uncertainty seriously. Oddly enough, statistics books rarely sound like it — they speak with the confidence of someone who has never had to think anything over. *The Regressive Backbone* keeps the two together: what the book says about uncertainty, it also does itself. Uncertainty is not a problem. It is contact with reality.

<!-- MIEKE: de knop heet in het (Nederlandse) boek "toon werknotities"; die staat er in het
     Nederlands bij, want dat is wat de lezer daar ziet. Of de Engelse hoofdstukken dezelfde
     knop krijgen, is nog niet besloten. "tweede leesniveau" — gekozen "a second way of
     reading"; alternatief "a second layer to read". -->
That is why every page of the book ends with a button: **show working notes** ([toon werknotities]{lang="nl"} in the Dutch). It opens two kinds of note. The first is the workbench — wordings still waiting to be chosen between, a figure that is still on its way. The second is the doubt, and that one is about you: *does the reader see here that this is about the population, or does it need to be sharper?* Under a question like that, the extra explanation is right there. If you follow, you simply read on; if you stall, you open the note and find exactly that piece. It is not a peek behind the scenes. It is a second way of reading.

<!-- MIEKE: "Blijf jij op zo'n plek even haken" — gekozen "get stuck there for a moment";
     alternatief "snag on a place like that". "Je staat naast de auteur in plaats van onder
     hem" — de "hem" is de auteur, zoals in het Nederlands. -->
And it does something else. Where the material is hard, the page now simply says so, in the words of someone who is still weighing up how to explain it. If you get stuck there for a moment, that is not down to you — that is where everyone's thinking stalls, the writer's included. You stand beside the author instead of beneath him. That is exactly where this book wants you.
